A truncated host name cannot redirect a request. Most names Python resolves come from configuration (API base URLs, notification and AI endpoints). The URLs users enter (VEX sources by a target's owner, advisory feeds and server lists by an admin) are fetched with httpx, which refuses a URL containing a null byte or any other control character before it connects; the public-host check (backend/app/services/http/public_host.py) may look up the shortened name, but no request follows. User-supplied scan targets are resolved by git, skopeo and the Go scanners after validate_scan_target has checked them, and the sidecar's own lookups go to fixed registry hosts.

The regression only weakens hashlib's algorithm checks when OpenSSL runs in FIPS mode. The images' OpenSSL is not configured for FIPS mode. Fixed in CPython 3.14.11, which the images pick up on rebuild.

A server can delete cookies of other domains from a shared http.cookiejar. The services' httpx clients keep such a jar, but nothing in it carries authority: every outbound request authenticates with headers (API keys, bearer tokens, http.extraHeader for git), never with cookies, so a deleted cookie changes nothing.
